From: Evan Brooks <evan@propulsionhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@propulsionhealth.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 15:22:00 -0500
Subject: Evaluating Redwood for Propulsion bakeoff — credits & timeline

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Propulsion is running a three-way bakeoff the week of Jan 10 to validate latency/cost on our generative summarization pipeline. We need to confirm what kind of evaluation support Redwood can provide:

- Trial credits or a stipend for a short benchmark run (ideally something that covers ~200k tokens)
- A short trial window extension (our engineering team wants an extra 3 weeks)
- Any compliance materials for procurement (SOC2 summary, data handling notes)

We have competitors participating and procurement will want the incentives documented. Can you share a formal proposal or MOU we can include in the RFP?

Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of ML Ops, Propulsion Health

Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood for Propulsion bakeoff — credits & timeline

Evan —

Appreciate the details and timeline. We can support Propulsion's bakeoff and here is what we typically offer for this type of competitive evaluation:

- 200,000 token evaluation credit tied to the PH-2026-0042 deal (usable over a 30-day evaluation window).
- One 3-week trial extension on top of the default trial period (starts when you first send traffic).
- We will provide a short SOC2 summary and a draft MOU for procurement to reference (attached).

A couple of important notes:
- Credits are for benchmarking/evaluation only and cannot be applied to production workloads.
- Credits cannot be combined with other incentive programs from Redwood (no stacking for the same account).

I've attached the SOC2 summary and a draft MOU. Marcus — can you add a short usage dashboard link and the instrumentation guide so they can measure token usage during the bakeoff?

Next steps:
1) Evan — confirm that the 200k token amount and 30-day window work for your team.
2) Procurement — if you want the MOU redlined, send back suggested edits and we can route to legal.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Aditya / Jordan — thanks, this is great news and I appreciate the quick turnaround. Two quick clarifications before we finalize: 

1) Attribution / confidentiality: procurement wants a short clause stating that Redwood's incentive is confidential between the parties for 90 days. Is that something you can accept?

2) Measurement: we need the daily token report in CSV and a read-only dashboard. Jordan / Marcus — can you confirm the export format and cadence?

3) Competitor stacking: procurement asked whether Redwood will participate in other incentives if competitors offer stipends. We understand your no-stacking rule — can you confirm whether that means Propulsion cannot accept competitor incentives simultaneously (we may need to disclose)?

If you can confirm these three items, procurement will draft the MOU redlines and we can turn the credits on the week of Jan 3.
